issues.main_description_html:
Connect the Editor to the New Mode System

Docs

Spec

2026-06-22-hover-area-label-design.md

Plan

2026-06-22-hover-area-label.md

Context

Tasks 2 and 3 taught the room layer and the label canvas how to behave differently per view mode. But neither system knows yet that the editor exists — they are waiting to be told which mode to use. Until the editor passes "editor" as its view mode, both systems continue to behave as they always have.

Goal

Update the 3D map view inside the editor so it activates editor-mode behaviour in both the room layer and the label canvas.

What We're Building

Two small additions to the component that renders the 3D map in the editor:

  1. Room layer receives viewMode: "editor" — this tells the layer to suppress all hover fill highlights. Rooms will no longer flash blue when the cursor passes over them while the designer is working.

  2. Label canvas receives viewMode: "editor" and the ID of whichever room is currently hovered — this tells the canvas to show only that room's label on hover, and nothing otherwise.

The hovered room ID is already tracked by the editor's existing state — no new data fetching or store changes are needed. It just needs to be passed through to the label canvas alongside the mode.

Why It Matters

Without this wiring, the editor ignores all the mode-aware logic built in Tasks 2 and 3. The designer would still see vivid blue hover flashes and a screen full of room labels — the same behaviour as today. This task is the switch that turns the new behaviour on for the editing context.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Hovering a room in the editor no longer produces a fill highlight on the room extrusion
  • Hovering a named room in the editor shows that room's label
  • Hovering a room without a name shows nothing
  • Moving the cursor off a room makes the label disappear immediately
  • Area labels are not visible in the editor when nothing is hovered
  • Existing editor behaviours — room selection, pin labels, level switching — are unaffected
  • The codebase builds, typechecks, and lints with zero new errors
  • The change is committed on its own

What Changes After This Task

The editor operates in editor mode. The preview overlay is still in default mode — Task 5 will wire that separately.

RESULT

The map-hook editor wiring (originally on Editor3DMapView) was reverted per product feedback — the 3D Map tab keeps its original all-labels behaviour. Hover-only labels were instead implemented where the editor actually renders: the engine.

  • 2D canvas (draw.ts + interactions.ts): tracks the room/area polygon under the cursor (highlightRoom / hoverManual) and draws a room's name label only when hovered or selected; a small dot marks every room at all times.
  • 3D scene (scene3d.ts): room label sprites are tracked and their visibility gated the same way; recolor() toggles them, so hovering in either view reveals the matching label.

Commits: f32b1f5, 2510173, 7e05c0a, e381a42, 6dc9164. Typecheck + ESLint clean. Merged to development (594af03).

issues.display_title: Issue #131: Teach the Label Canvas How to Behave Per Mode
issues.main_description_html:
Teach the Label Canvas How to Behave Per Mode

Docs

Spec

2026-06-22-hover-area-label-design.md

Plan

2026-06-22-hover-area-label.md

Context

The system that draws room name labels on the 3D map currently shows all labels at all times, regardless of whether the user is editing, previewing, or zoomed far out. In the editor this means every room's name is always on screen, which clutters the workspace. In the preview it means labels pile up when the map is zoomed out to show the whole building.

Goal

Give the label canvas a "view mode" setting so labels appear at the right time, in the right context, at the right scale — adapting automatically to whether the user is editing or exploring.

What We're Building

Three distinct label behaviours, selected by a new optional view mode setting:

Editor mode — Only the currently hovered room's label is drawn, and only if that room has a name. The label appears as the cursor moves over it and vanishes when the cursor leaves. No other labels are visible. This gives the designer a clean canvas to work on, with names available on demand rather than always in the way.

Preview and map mode (zoomed in) — All named room labels are drawn at once, spread across the floor plan with the existing declutter logic that prevents overlapping labels at high zoom levels. This is the existing behaviour, preserved for the zoomed-in experience.

Preview and map mode (zoomed out) — When the user zooms out past a set threshold (zoom level 17.5), individual room labels disappear and a single building name label appears at the geographical centre of the floor plan instead. This keeps the map readable at distance — one landmark label rather than a screen full of small text. Zooming back in restores the individual labels immediately.

The zoom threshold is tracked automatically via a listener — the canvas repaints as the user zooms, so the transition between building name and room labels is seamless.

When no view mode is provided, the canvas behaves exactly as it does today.

Why It Matters

Room labels are only useful in context. A designer mid-edit does not need all labels visible at once — they need to be able to glance at a room name without the screen being filled with text. A visitor zoomed out to see the whole building cannot read dozens of small labels overlapping at that scale — they need a single orientation anchor. This task gives each context exactly what it needs.

Acceptance Criteria

  • In editor mode, only the hovered room's label is visible; all other labels are hidden
  • In editor mode, rooms without a name show no label even when hovered
  • In preview/map mode at high zoom, all named room labels are shown with declutter (existing behaviour)
  • In preview/map mode when zoomed out past the threshold, individual labels disappear and the building name appears at the floor plan centre
  • Zooming back in past the threshold restores the individual room labels
  • The selected-room pin label (the teardrop pin beside a selected room) is not affected — it always renders in all modes
  • Components that do not pass a view mode see no change in behaviour
  • The codebase builds, typechecks, and lints with zero new errors
  • The change is committed on its own

What Changes After This Task

The label canvas understands modes and zoom. Task 4 (editor wiring) will activate editor-mode labels; Task 5 (preview wiring) will activate preview-mode labels and pass the building name.

RESULT

Added viewMode, hoveredAreaId, buildingName to useFloorPlanLabels (src/lib/map/useFloorPlanLabels.ts): editor = hovered room's label only; preview/map = all labels with declutter when zoomed in, single building-name label at the floor-plan centre below zoom 17.5 (tracked via a zoom listener). An undefined viewMode keeps the original behaviour (all labels always), so the Map tab is unaffected. The selected-room pin label and the point/safety marker draw are untouched.

issues.display_title: Issue #130: Teach the Room Layer How to Behave Per Mode
issues.main_description_html:
Teach the Room Layer How to Behave Per Mode

Docs

Spec

2026-06-22-hover-area-label-design.md

Plan

2026-06-22-hover-area-label.md

Context

The system that renders rooms on the 3D map — drawing their walls, fills, and hover highlights — currently applies the same vivid blue hover fill regardless of whether the user is an editor working on a floor plan or a visitor exploring a published space. There is no concept of context: the layer just highlights whenever something is hovered.

Goal

Give the room layer a "view mode" setting so it can suppress the hover fill entirely in the editor, and switch to the new subtle colour in the preview, without changing anything for consumers that do not pass a mode.

What We're Building

A new optional setting on the room layer called view mode, which accepts one of three values: editor, preview, or map.

When view mode is set to editor, the layer never applies a fill highlight on hover, no matter which room the cursor is over. The room shapes stay visually neutral so the designer is not distracted while working.

When view mode is set to preview or map, the layer swaps the hover fill from the standard vivid blue to the subtle light blue-grey defined in Task 1 — the same quiet tone used by Mappedin. The fill appears only on named rooms (that logic lives in Task 5).

When no view mode is provided (the default), the layer behaves exactly as it does today, so nothing breaks for any component that has not yet been updated.

The switch also applies correctly when the map reloads its style or the user toggles between 2D and 3D view — the layer re-applies the right colour immediately rather than falling back to the default.

Why It Matters

Without this separation, every context gets the same hover treatment. That means a designer working carefully on room boundaries sees a distracting flash of blue every time the cursor passes over a room, and a preview visitor sees a louder highlight than the product's visual tone calls for. This task draws the line between those two contexts at the source — the layer renderer — so everything built on top of it inherits the correct behaviour automatically.

Acceptance Criteria

  • In editor mode, no fill colour appears on hovered rooms under any circumstances
  • In preview and map mode, hovered rooms show the subtle light blue-grey fill instead of the vivid blue
  • Components that do not pass a view mode see no change in behaviour
  • The paint correction applies after style reloads and 2D/3D mode switches — not just on initial load
  • The codebase builds, typechecks, and lints with zero new errors
  • The change is committed on its own

What Changes After This Task

The room layer understands modes. Task 4 (editor wiring) and Task 5 (preview wiring) will pass the correct mode to activate this behaviour in each context.

RESULT

Added viewMode: "editor" | "preview" | "map" to useFloorPlanLayer (src/lib/map/useFloorPlanLayer.ts): editor suppresses the hover highlight entirely; preview/map swap the vivid-blue fill for the subtle hover colour (Task 1) via a new applyHighlightPaint, re-applied after style reloads and 2D/3D switches. Adapted to the current applyHighlight(map, string[]) signature (editor passes []). The Map tab is wired to viewMode="map" so its hover fill uses the subtle colour too.

issues.display_title: Issue #129: Establish the Subtle Hover Colour Values
issues.main_description_html:
Establish the Subtle Hover Colour Values

Docs

Spec

2026-06-22-hover-area-label-design.md

Plan

2026-06-22-hover-area-label.md

Context

The app currently uses a single vivid blue when highlighting a room on hover. That colour works for the selection state (clicking a room) but is too strong for a gentle hover interaction — especially in the public-facing preview where the intent is to feel subtle and welcoming rather than sharp and tool-like.

Before any view-mode logic can be wired up, the two new colour values need to exist as named constants that the rest of the code can reference by name.

Goal

Define a very light blue-grey colour and its matching transparency level as named values, so that every part of the system that needs a subtle hover effect can use the same consistent shade without anyone hard-coding a colour string.

What We're Building

Two new named values added to the file that holds all the map colour definitions:

  • A subtle hover fill colour — a very light blue-grey (#e8f0fe), the same quiet tone used by Mappedin's hover style.
  • A subtle hover opacity — 0.18, just enough to register as interactive without drawing the eye.

These sit alongside the existing colour constants (wall colour, area background, selection outline, etc.) and are exported so the layer rendering system can import and use them.

Why It Matters

Colour decisions made in one place are easy to tune and impossible to get out of sync. If the preview hover colour ever needs to change — say, to match a new brand palette — one edit here updates every consumer automatically. Hard-coding the same hex string in three places would mean hunting for all of them later.

Acceptance Criteria

  • The two new colour constants exist and are exported from the colour definitions file
  • No existing colour constants are changed or removed
  • The codebase builds and typechecks with zero new errors
  • The change is committed on its own so the colour decision is independently traceable

What Changes After This Task

The subtle hover colours are available for Task 2 to import and apply to the hover highlight layer.

RESULT

Added HOVER_FILL_COLOR_SUBTLE and HOVER_FILL_OPACITY_SUBTLE to src/lib/map/layer-definitions.ts, exported for the per-mode room-layer hover paint. Values later tuned by the product owner. No existing constants changed.

Commit: eeb8999 (constants), 78027ea (tuning). Typecheck + ESLint clean. Merged to development (594af03).
